b: When I started weighing my food, I realized just how much I was undereating when I was trying to eat healthy. I had this idea in my head of what a healthy portion should look like, and I was consistently serving myself less than I actually needed. I’d finish meals feeling somewhat unsatisfied, get hungry again later in the day, and eventually end up overeating because I was so hungry. Once I started weighing my food and understanding portions better, I realized I could actually eat significantly more than I thought while still staying within my calorie goals.
It’s made eating healthy so much more enjoyable because I’m no longer unnecessarily restricting myself at meals and then fighting hunger for the rest of the day.

I just thought I’d share because food scales are almost always discussed as a tool for portion control, but for me, they’ve been just as valuable for making sure I’m eating enough to feel satisfaction. Don’t get me wrong, I’m sure if I weighed my food from restaurants or eating out I’d have the opposite feeling, but when I’m cooking for myself at home it makes me realize how much more I can eat and it feels so liberating.
